t: "There is only one place where he could hide: the old lead mine, in the very heart of the moor."

t: "He will get there, but he will never get out, for in the fog he will not see the stakes we set up together to show him the way to Grimpen Mire."

t: It is a pity I could not pull them up today, for then he would have been at your mercy...

t: Meanwhile we left Lestrade at his post at Merripit House, and Sir Henry and I returned to Baskerville Hall.

t: We sent for Doctor Mortimer.

t: When the baronet had somewhat recovered, under the care of that excellent physician he set out on a journey round the world to regain his mental balance.

t: He returned morally and physically sound.

t: I am approaching the end of this strange story; I have tried to pass on to my readers the fears that haunted us for so long and ended so tragically.

t: On the day after the events I have described, the fog had lifted, and under Mrs. Stapleton's guidance we managed to reach the point from which the path led out onto the moor.

t: The unhappy woman, with an eagerness that spoke of the deep wound inflicted on her by the man who had ruined her life and trodden her honour in the mire, tried to put us on the track of him.

t: Only once did we see a sign that someone had passed along this dangerous path.

t: Holding this shoe, he was on the trail of Sir Henry...

t: Having passed the deepest of the bogs, we searched for the print of feet on what was now firm ground.

t: In vain. If the testimony of the earth was trustworthy, Stapleton had not reached the island towards which he was striving through the fog.

t: His bones lie somewhere in the impenetrable quagmire…

t: But we found plenty of traces of him on the island where he had hidden the dog.

t: "Look! This is Mortimer's favourite!"

t: He might indeed have kept it in the outhouse at Merripit House, but that would have been risky.

t: The ointment in this tin is, no doubt, a mixture of sulphur and phosphorus, with which the dog was smeared.

t: No wonder that Seldon fled screaming.

t: It was a hellish idea!

t: The point was not only to terrify the victim, but also to hamper the investigation, for the dog, breathing fire, filled the surrounding peasants with superstitious fear and took away their inclination to hunt down the monster.

o: Mówiłem ci to już raz w Londynie, Watson, a teraz powtarzam, że Stapleton był najniebezpieczniejszym łotrem, z jakim zdarzyło mi się spotkać w życiu.
t: I've told you that once already in London, Watson, and I repeat it now: Stapleton was the most dangerous villain I have ever encountered in my life.
